main_text.p: per accidens optimè explicatur hoc axio-mate: Ens additum ei, quod omnem perfe-ctionem suo generi debitam actu obtinet, efficit Unum per accidens. Itaque accidens additum substantiæ, efficit Unum per acci-dens, quia non est perfectio debita sub-stantiæ, ut est substantia: at Forma addita materiæ efficit Unum per se, quia Forma materiæ debetur ad constituendam substantiam. Similiter acervus lapidum est Unum per aggregationem, sive per accidens, quia lapis unus non pertinet ad perfectionem alterius; At homo licet ex diversis partibus constet, per se tamen Unum est, quia pars unaquæque in suo genere destinata est ad perfectionem majorem, sive ad constitutionem Totius, atque insuper cæteris partibus sic adjungitur, ut ex omnibus constituatur continuum quidpiam.

page.notes: The initial "A" is a large decorative letter, joined to "D" to give "AD". Printed "Convenientia}" carries a brace-like mark after the word at the end of the first line of the thesis paragraph; it is not text and is not transcribed. Source spelling "Vnitatem", "Vnum", "Vnitas" with initial V was changed to Unitatem, Unum, Unitas per the u/v rule. "Diverfitate" and "Diverfitas" with long s were read as Diversitate and Diversitas. Some italic letters in the title are heavily decorated and are read with some uncertainty, but the words are clear. No marginal notes or footnotes are printed on this page.
